title: Markets: Sunday 1 November

morning.session_note: Weekend edition · what's new since Saturday, with the week ahead
summary: Iran sent a delegation to Doha and its foreign minister said a Qatar-brokered plan would reopen Hormuz within two days if Iran's conditions are met, while Secretary of State Rubio said Trump "hasn't made a decision" on new strikes ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/31/iran-fm-says-us-outreach-a-positive-step-as-delegation-in-qatar-for-talks), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6407713967112)). Three sources told Reuters that core OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to keep December output targets steady when they meet on Sunday ([MarketScreener](https://au.marketscreener.com/news/opec-agrees-in-principle-to-keep-oil-output-targets-steady-in-december-sources-say-ce785fd8db81f220)).

China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October from 50.1, back below the 50 line that separates growth from contraction, with new orders and output both shrinking ([NBS](https://www.stats.gov.cn/xxgk/sjfb/zxfb2020/202610/t20261031_1965718.html)). China takes 75% of the world's seaborne iron ore, according to the Australian Government's Resources and Energy Quarterly ([REQ](https://www.industry.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/resources-and-energy-quarterly-september-2026.pdf)), so its factory demand is watched closely in Australia.

The week ahead is crowded: an RBA decision on Tuesday where markets priced a 78% chance of a hike at Friday's close ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)), the US midterms the same day, a likely Bank of England hike on Thursday and US payrolls early Saturday Sydney time ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).

cards.headline: Record election-day fuel prices frame Tuesday's US midterms
cards.takeaway: Petrol and diesel prices are a central campaign issue, and options markets are pricing a larger-than-usual move after the vote.
cards.key_figure: US petrol US$4.20/gal, diesel US$6.32/gal (GasBuddy, 30 Oct)
cards.new_since_last_issue: GasBuddy's fuel-price figures and the Republican-linked stock basket data are new; the Polymarket odds were covered on Saturday.
cards.what_happened: US petrol averaged US$4.20 a gallon on Friday, nearly 40% above a year earlier, and diesel US$6.32, up about 70%, according to GasBuddy, which expects the highest election-day prices on record ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/trump-gas-diesel-price-midterm-election.html)). The White House said fuel prices will "drop drastically" once the conflict ends and that inflation-adjusted prices were higher around past elections. A UBS basket of stocks linked to Republican policies has fallen since peaking in August, Bloomberg reported ([Bloomberg via Moneycontrol](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/wall-street-braces-for-market-volatility-as-democrats-eye-control-of-congress-in-us-midterm-elections-14065116.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Trump has said he will not resume strikes on Iran before the vote, and CNBC reported that the market is pricing the risk of what happens after Tuesday ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/trump-gas-diesel-price-midterm-election.html)). Options imply a move of about 1.2 times a typical day for 4 November, roughly 20% larger than usual but broadly in line with past midterms, according to Man Group ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/us-midterms-election-wall-street-options-markets.html)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: S&P 500 7,580.1 (−0.6% for the week), Nasdaq 25,437.0 (−2.0% for the week), VIX 19.42.

competing_views.view: Said an escalation with Iran could push fuel prices higher just ahead of Thanksgiving.
Flagged a contested count as a risk that could extend volatility beyond election night.

cards.what_to_watch: Results from Wednesday morning Sydney time; any White House decision on Iran after the vote.

cards.headline: Payrolls, ISM surveys and chip earnings test the Fed hike case
cards.takeaway: Forecasters expect modest jobs growth and firm factory activity, while Apple, AMD and Qualcomm report after last week's tech selloff.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Barclays' below-consensus payrolls forecast and the earnings line-up are new; the consensus figures repeat Saturday's calendar.
cards.what_happened: Forecasters expect October payrolls of 55,000 with unemployment steady at 4.2%; Barclays forecasts 50,000 and a dip in unemployment to 4.1%. ISM manufacturing is seen at 54.7 and services at 54.7 ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)). Apple, Qualcomm and AMD report during the week ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-midterms-meet-earnings-4986208)).
cards.why_it_matters: Markets priced about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike before the week, according to Reuters ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-midterms-meet-earnings-4986208)), so payrolls and the ISM surveys are the main data tests of that pricing. The Treasury's quarterly refunding on Wednesday US time feeds through to long-dated yields, according to Newsquawk ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.what_to_watch: ISM manufacturing at about 2am Tuesday Sydney time; payrolls at about 12:30am Saturday.

cards.headline: RBA expected to lift rates to 4.85% on Tuesday
cards.takeaway: All four major banks expect a 25 bp hike to the highest cash rate since 2008; weekend reporting has turned to whether December's budget update will support the RBA.
cards.key_figure: Cash rate 4.60%; ASX futures 78% hike odds (30 Oct close)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Weekend reporting on fiscal pressure ahead of the December budget update is new; the pricing is unchanged as markets were shut.
cards.what_happened: ASX 30-day futures priced a 78% chance of a hike to 4.85% at Friday's close ([RBA Watch](https://rbawatch.com/rba-meeting/november-2026)). ANZ, CBA, NAB and Westpac all expect a hike, AAP reported ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)). Focus is shifting to whether December's mid-year budget update cuts spending to support the RBA, the ABC reported on Sunday ([ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-01/interest-rate-myefo-albanese-armstrong-analysis-economy/107327460)).
cards.why_it_matters: A hike would take the cash rate to a level last seen in 2008. The RBA also releases new forecasts in its Statement on Monetary Policy, after the September-quarter trimmed mean rose 1.0% against the RBA's 0.8% forecast ([AAP](https://aapnews.aap.com.au/news/the-figures-to-watch-ahead-of-melbourne-cup-rate-call)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: AU 2-year 4.95% (+3 bp for the week, as at 28 Oct), AUD/USD 0.7040 (+0.5% for the week).

competing_views.view: In September she said further hikes might not be needed if inflation declined, but has since said inflation remains far too high and upside risks are materialising (as summarised by Newsquawk).

cards.what_to_watch: Decision at 2:30pm Tuesday, media conference at 3:30pm; Westpac full-year results Monday ([Westpac](https://www.westpac.com.au/about-westpac/investor-centre/events-and-presentations/presentations-agm/)) and NAB's on Thursday ([NAB](https://www.nab.com.au/about-us/shareholder-centre)).

cards.headline: China's factory activity shrank in October
cards.takeaway: The official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3, with new orders and output contracting; services held at 50 while the wider non-manufacturing index slipped to 49.7.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Released Saturday 31 October, after the last issue.
cards.what_happened: China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1. The output index fell to 49.8 from 51.7 and new orders to 49.4 from 50.5. The non-manufacturing PMI was 49.7, with services at 50.0, and the composite fell 1.0 point to 49.7 ([NBS](https://www.stats.gov.cn/xxgk/sjfb/zxfb2020/202610/t20261031_1965718.html), [China Daily](https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202610/31/WS6ae561fbe4b06d4aa05663b0.html)). NBS chief statistician Huo Lihui attributed the fall partly to demand brought forward before the National Day holiday and a complex international environment ([NBS](https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/sjjd/202610/t20261031_1965719.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: China imports 75% of the world's seaborne iron ore, and the Australian Government links falling iron ore prices partly to weaker Chinese demand ([Resources and Energy Quarterly](https://www.industry.gov.au/sites/default/files/2026-10/resources-and-energy-quarterly-september-2026.pdf)). Input prices eased to 56.8 from 60.8; Huo said this reflected lower prices for some non-ferrous metals, while price indices for oil-processing industries stayed above 60 as crude prices rose ([NBS](https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/sjjd/202610/t20261031_1965719.html)). China's NPC Standing Committee meets this week; its agenda has no fiscal items, according to Newsquawk ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.market_reaction: Iron ore price unavailable in the data feed; markets reopen Monday.
cards.what_to_watch: Any fiscal items added to the NPC Standing Committee agenda (2–6 November).

cards.headline: BoE, Riksbank and Norges Bank decisions follow the RBA this week
cards.takeaway: The Bank of England and Riksbank are expected to raise rates and Norges Bank to hold, in a week Reuters said markets expect several hikes.
cards.key_figure: BoE expected +25 bp; Riksbank expected to 2.00%
cards.new_since_last_issue: The Riksbank, Norges Bank and euro-area inflation previews are new; weekly yield totals are shown for reference only.
cards.what_happened: The Bank of England is expected to start a tightening cycle with a 25 bp hike on Thursday, the Riksbank to raise its rate to 2.00% on Wednesday and Norges Bank to hold at 4.50% ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)). Euro area flash inflation on Wednesday follows 3.8% in September, its highest since September 2023 ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.why_it_matters: Markets expect the RBA, Riksbank and BoE to hike as central banks respond to growing inflation risks, and Norges Bank has already hiked twice, Reuters reported ([Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/take-five-midterms-meet-earnings-4986208)).
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard (week to Friday): US 2-year 4.56% (−13 bp), US 10-year 4.94% (−6 bp); AU 2-year 4.95% (+3 bp) and AU 10-year 5.21% (−7 bp), both for the week to 28 Oct, the latest RBA data.
cards.what_to_watch: BoE vote split on Thursday night Sydney time; US Treasury refunding early Thursday Sydney time.

cards.headline: Iran sends team to Doha as US keeps strike option open
cards.takeaway: Iran says a mediated plan could reopen Hormuz in two days if its conditions are met; the US says no decision on new strikes has been made.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Iran's response to the US letter, its Hormuz conditions and Rubio's remarks are all from Saturday.
cards.what_happened: Foreign Minister Araghchi said the US outreach was "a positive step" but Iran sees "no need to meet with the Americans at this stage". He said talks with Qatari mediators had cut the time to implement Iran's Hormuz plan to two days, on conditions including lifting sanctions, reducing US forces, restoring oil waivers and releasing frozen funds ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/31/iran-fm-says-us-outreach-a-positive-step-as-delegation-in-qatar-for-talks)). Rubio said Trump "hasn't made a decision" on resuming military action and "prefers to solve it diplomatically" ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/video/6407713967112), [The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/us/2026/10/31/us-iran-strikes-g20-rubio/)). Iran's armed forces chief said any attack would draw a response with no geographical limits ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/31/iran-fm-says-us-outreach-a-positive-step-as-delegation-in-qatar-for-talks)).
cards.why_it_matters: US officials have warned allies to prepare for possible strikes after Tuesday's midterms, though Trump has not announced a final decision ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/qatar-iran-us-talks-mediation.html)). Oil markets are pricing the risk of what happens after the vote, CNBC reported separately ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/trump-gas-diesel-price-midterm-election.html)).
cards.market_reaction: Oil: January Brent, the active contract, settled at US$113.43 on Friday (CNBC); see the Brent price comparison in the next card.

competing_views.view: Called the US outreach "a positive step" but said Iran sees "no need to meet with the Americans at this stage".

competing_views.who: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
competing_views.view: Said the US would be open to a diplomatic solution that does not endanger US security, while Trump has made no decision on further military action.

cards.what_to_watch: Any US response to Iran's conditions, and White House signals after the midterm vote.

cards.headline: OPEC+ set to hold output as Gulf shipping attacks rise
cards.takeaway: Three sources told Reuters core OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to keep December targets steady at Sunday's meeting, while attacks on ships and Saudi territory continued.
cards.key_figure: Just over 30 shipping attacks in October (UKMTO)
cards.new_since_last_issue: The OPEC+ sources report, UKMTO's October tally, CENTCOM's blockade update and Saturday's drone interception over Riyadh are new.
cards.what_happened: Seven core OPEC+ members have agreed in principle to keep December output targets steady when they meet online on Sunday, three sources told Reuters; most Gulf members are still pumping well below their targets ([MarketScreener](https://au.marketscreener.com/news/opec-agrees-in-principle-to-keep-oil-output-targets-steady-in-december-sources-say-ce785fd8db81f220)). The UK's maritime security agency counted just over 30 attacks on shipping in October, double September's, and CENTCOM said the US blockade has redirected 144 vessels ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-diplomacy-threat-resume-attacks/)). Saudi air defences intercepted a drone over the Riyadh region on Saturday ([AFP via The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/saudi-arabia-shoots-down-drone-in-riyadh-houthis-yemen-october-31-2026/article71648572.ece)).
cards.why_it_matters: Most Gulf members are already producing well below their targets, according to the Reuters report. Treasury Secretary Bessent said transit levels are back to pre-conflict levels excluding Iranian barrels, while UKMTO's tally shows attacks rising ([CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/iran-war-us-trump-diplomacy-threat-resume-attacks/)).
cards.market_reaction: Brent: the expiring December contract settled at US$117.64 (+2.4%) on Friday and the active January contract at US$113.43 (+US$2.63) (CNBC).
cards.what_to_watch: The official OPEC+ statement on Sunday, and tanker incidents around Tuesday's US vote.

cards.headline: Ukraine's refinery strikes resume, adding to diesel tightness
cards.takeaway: Russia confirmed attacks on three refineries after a pause, keeping pressure on global diesel supply.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Not covered in Saturday's issue; Russia confirmed the strikes on 30 October.
cards.what_happened: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Novak said Ukraine attacked three refineries and a gas-chemical complex on 30 October, after "a brief pause", according to TASS as reported by the Kyiv Independent. A Ukrainian drone maker said the Novokuybyshevsk refinery's diesel unit was hit; Kyiv had not commented ([Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/russian-oil-refinery-reportedly-attacked-amid-renewed-ukrainian-strikes-on-energy-infrastructure/)). Novak also said the Ukrainian attacks would hurt global diesel supply ([Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/week-in-focus-2nd-6th-november-2026-highlights-include-us-midterm-election-nfp-ism-pmis-rba-boe-and-ez-cpi-)).
cards.why_it_matters: Exxon's chief executive called diesel the key crunch point in fuel markets, CNBC reported. The US agreed a deal for Russia to export about 6 million barrels of diesel through November, which analysts said is too small to move prices much ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/trump-gas-diesel-price-midterm-election.html)).
cards.what_to_watch: Further refinery strikes and any US pressure on Kyiv after the midterms.

cards.headline: Binance says it has covered 90% of US$6.3 billion hack
cards.takeaway: The exchange restored backing for its top 10 tokens and aims to reopen withdrawals on Sunday.
cards.new_since_last_issue: The size of the theft, the 90% coverage and the withdrawal timetable are new since Saturday.
cards.what_happened: Binance said it has restored backing for about 90% of the roughly US$6.3 billion stolen from its hot wallets, using its user protection fund, part of its futures insurance fund and its treasury, and plans to resume withdrawals on Sunday subject to security checks; CNBC noted this is not the same as recovering 90% from the attacker ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-coverage-withdrawals.html), [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckpdg3ql4169o)). Blockchain analytics firms have linked the theft to North Korea's Lazarus Group; North Korea has denied involvement in past attacks.
cards.why_it_matters: The theft is believed to be the largest crypto hack on record, ahead of the US$1.5 billion Bybit theft in 2025, the BBC reported. Binance said the remaining 10% is in less liquid tokens outside its top 10, which may take longer to source ([BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckpdg3ql4169o), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-coverage-withdrawals.html)).

watchlist.note: Up 22.6% for the week to A$1.79, recovering part of the previous Friday's 29% fall on US fraud losses. The rebound began Monday after UBS called the selloff "an overreaction" and Macquarie kept its A$3.50 target, while Citi and Jefferies were more cautious. It fell 3.8% on Friday after Thursday's jump; Morningstar that day kept its A$3.50 fair value, saying investors are too pessimistic about the fraud hit. No new ASX filings since Friday.

Up 2.0% for the week to A$200.73, including 1.6% on Friday, as the ASX healthcare index rose and has gained 38% since late July, according to Market Index. CSL held its AGM on Tuesday and named Gordon Naylor as next chair; its only filing since is a buy-back update.

Up 0.9% for the week to A$11.35, with no company announcement since 20 October. It rose 0.4% on Friday as consumer discretionary stocks snapped a four-day losing streak, though the sector was still down about 2% for the week, according to Market Index.

Unchanged for the week at A$2.21 after a 0.5% fall on Friday, when it missed the discretionary rebound. IDP's filings were buy-back updates, a substantial holder exiting on 28 October and two final director's interest notices; none was price-sensitive, and we found no report explaining the moves.

ZIP.note: Up 22.6% for the week to A$1.79, recovering part of the previous Friday's 29% fall on US fraud losses. The rebound began Monday after UBS called the selloff "an overreaction" and Macquarie kept its A$3.50 target, while Citi and Jefferies were more cautious. It fell 3.8% on Friday after Thursday's jump; Morningstar that day kept its A$3.50 fair value, saying investors are too pessimistic about the fraud hit. No new ASX filings since Friday.
